bug_description.normalized: The staged 21-byte PoC `{"Body""  "}"Type"15 ` tokenizes into five JSMN tokens: a root object with `size == 2`, the in-object strings `"Body"` and `"  "`, then the later top-level `"Type"` and `15` tokens after the closing brace. `Variant_decodeJson()` first calls `lookAheadForKey("Type")`; because `searchObjectForKeyRec()` interprets the root object's `size` as a two-entry object walk, it skips from the first in-object string to the later `"Type"` token and parses `15` as the Variant type. A later `lookAheadForKey("Body")` resolves the first in-object string token as the body, so the scalar Variant dispatches to `ByteString_decodeJson()`. `UA_unbase64()` then decodes the 2-character body with `pad == 0`, computes `*flen == 1`, allocates one byte, but executes neither its 4-character loop nor its padding tails, so it returns a one-byte heap buffer without initializing `bin[0]`. `decodeFields()` still consumes the later `"Type"` token, `UA_decodeJson()` returns `GOOD`, and the fuzzer reaches `UA_calcSizeJson()`. Re-encoding the scalar ByteString passes that one-byte buffer to `UA_base64()`, whose `pad == 2` tail reads `bin[0]` at `deps/base64.c:105`, producing the saved MemorySanitizer use-of-uninitialized-value report. The fix replaces the vulnerable base64 implementation.

source.description: First project-code statement on the witnessed vulnerable path that turns attacker-controlled token metadata into the loop bound for the malformed object walk.
source.value_from: Because the missing `:` after `"Body"` leaves both in-object strings as direct children of the still-open root object, the exact 21-byte PoC `{"Body""  "}"Type"15 ` tokenizes as `tokenArray[0] = JSMN_OBJECT(size=2)`, `tokenArray[1] = "Body"`, `tokenArray[2] = "  "`, `tokenArray[3] = "Type"`, and `tokenArray[4] = 15`. This statement reads the attacker-shaped root `size` into `objectCount`, creating the two-iteration bound that later produces both `searchResultType = 4` and `searchResultBody = 2`.

sink.description: MSAN crash site. On the witnessed path `byteNo` is still 0 and this line reads `bin[0]` from the one-byte buffer returned by `UA_unbase64()` without any prior initialization.

root_cause.description: The decode helper allocates output based on `*flen`, but for `len == 2` and `pad == 0` none of its write paths execute. It still returns the heap buffer as though one decoded byte had been produced, leaving `bin[0]` uninitialized for later re-encoding.

tainted_value_origin.description: The uninitialized byte consumed at the sink originates from this heap allocation. On the witnessed path `len == 2` and `pad == 0`, so `*flen` becomes 1 and `malloc(1)` allocates the single output byte before any decode stores occur.

parser_admitted.description: The exact PoC tokenizes into five tokens whose first token is still a `JSMN_OBJECT`, so the top-level object check falls through even though later `"Type"` and `15` tokens remain after the closing brace.

decode_accepted.description: After `decodeFields()` consumes token1/token2 as `Body` and token3/token4 as the skipped `Type` field, `parseCtx.index == parseCtx.tokenCount == 5`, so the post-decode sanity check accepts the malformed token stream and `UA_decodeJson()` returns `GOOD`.

coarse_trace.summary: `searchObjectForKeyRec()` reads the malformed root object's `size == 2` as a two-entry object walk, yielding `searchResultType = 4` from the later `"Type"` / `15` tokens and `searchResultBody = 2` from the in-object two-space string.

`Variant_decodeJson()` parses `Type == 15`, resolves the built-in ByteString type, classifies the `Body` token as a non-null scalar string, and sets up `decodeFields()` to decode only `Type` and `Body` from the malformed root object.

`decodeFields()` uses the same `objectCount == 2` to decode token2 through `ByteString_decodeJson()`, then consume the later `"Type"` / `15` tokens without reparsing them, so `UA_decodeJson()` returns `GOOD` and the fuzzer reaches `UA_calcSizeJson()`.
`UA_unbase64()` computes `flen == 1` for the 2-character body, allocates one byte, but initializes none of it because neither the main loop nor the padding tails execute.
After successful decode, `UA_calcSizeJson()` re-encodes the scalar ByteString Variant and routes its body to `ByteString_encodeJson()`.
`UA_base64()` handles the one-byte ByteString via its `pad == 2` tail path and reads `bin[0]` from the unwritten heap buffer, matching the saved MemorySanitizer report.

fine_trace.note: The exact PoC token stream makes the root token a `JSMN_OBJECT` whose stored `size` is 2, while later top-level tokens `"Type"` and `15` still remain after the closing brace. This read copies the attacker-shaped root `size` into `objectCount`, creating the two-iteration bound that later walks from the in-object body string to the later out-of-object type tokens.

During the first `lookAheadForKey(UA_JSONKEY_TYPE)` call, iteration 0 compares token1 `"Body"` against `"Type"` and misses; lines 2274-2285 then skip token2 and advance `parseCtx->index` to token3. Iteration 1 compares token3 `"Type"`, matches, increments once more, and stores `searchResultType = 4`, the index of primitive `15`. `lookAheadForKey()` then restores `parseCtx->index` to its original value.

At the recovered value token, `size` is 2 and `tokenArray[searchResultType].type` is `JSMN_PRIMITIVE`, so the guard passes and `atoiUnsigned()` parses the attacker bytes `15` into `idTypeDecoded == 15`.

The parsed numeric type is wrapped in `UA_NODEID_NUMERIC(0, 15)`, resolved through `UA_findDataType()`, and stored in `dst->type`. On the witnessed path this is the built-in ByteString type later dispatched through `ByteString_decodeJson()` and `ByteString_encodeJson()` in the saved stacks.

The later `lookAheadForKey(UA_JSONKEY_BODY)` reuses the same `objectCount == 2`, but now the first key token already matches `"Body"`. The helper therefore stores `searchResultBody = 2`, the index of the two-space string token, and `lookAheadForKey()` restores `parseCtx->index` afterward.

At token index 2, `bodyToken.type` is `JSMN_STRING`, not `JSMN_ARRAY`, and it is not the primitive `null`, so `isArray` stays false and `isBodyNull` stays false. The Variant therefore represents a scalar, non-null body string.

Because `!isArray`, `!isBodyNull`, and `bodyType->typeKind != UA_DATATYPEKIND_EXTENSIONOBJECT`, `Variant_decodeJson()` allocates one scalar body object and invokes `decodeFields()` with exactly two entries, `Type` and `Body`.

Inside `decodeFields()`, the same root `size` becomes `objectCount == 2`. On outer iteration 0, token1 `"Body"` matches `entries[1].fieldName`, `parseCtx->index` advances to token2, and the stored body decoder is invoked through `entries[1].function`, which dispatches to `ByteString_decodeJson()` for the ByteString `membertype` from step 4.

At `parseCtx->index == 2`, `GET_TOKEN` materializes the exact body string `"  "`; `tokenSize == 2`, the empty-body fast path is not taken, and `UA_unbase64()` receives the 2-character, unpadded input.

For the two-space body token, neither of the last two characters is `'='`, so `pad` stays 0. With `len == 2`, line 139 computes `*flen == 1`, and line 140 allocates the single heap byte that MSAN later reports as the origin.

Root cause. With `len == 2` and `pad == 0`, the main 4-character loop condition `charNo <= len - 4 - pad` is false at `charNo == 0`, and both tail branches `pad == 1` and `pad == 2` are also false. `cb` stays 0, so the one-byte allocation is returned without any store to `bin[0]`.

The byte-string decoder treats the decode as successful, publishes the returned buffer as a scalar `UA_ByteString` with `length == 1`, and because `moveToken` is true advances `parseCtx->index` from the body token to 3. The Variant now aliases a one-byte buffer whose only byte is still uninitialized.

Outer iteration 1 begins with `parseCtx->index == 3`; token3 `"Type"` matches `entries[0]`, `parseCtx->index` advances to token4 `15`, and because `entries[0].function` is `NULL` line 3110 advances once more to `parseCtx->index == 5` without reparsing the type. `decodeFields()` returns `GOOD` after consuming exactly the two entries implied by `objectCount == 2`.

After the two `decodeFields()` iterations, `parseCtx.index == parseCtx.tokenCount == 5`, so the post-decode sanity check does not reject the malformed token stream. `ret` stays `GOOD`, `UA_decodeJson()` returns success, and the fuzzer falls through its `if(retval != UA_STATUSCODE_GOOD) return 0;` guard to `UA_calcSizeJson()`.

The decoded Variant is still scalar because `isArray` stayed false in step 6, and its built-in type is ByteString from step 4. In `UA_calcSizeJson(..., true)`, the reversible `!isArray` branch forwards `src->data` and `src->type` to `encodeJsonInternal()`, which dispatches to `ByteString_encodeJson()`.
The byte-string encoder receives a non-null body with `src->length == 1`, so it calls `UA_base64()` on the same one-byte buffer returned by `UA_unbase64()`.

Sink. For `len == 1`, `UA_base64()` computes `modulusLen == 1` and `pad == 2`, skips the 3-byte loop, and immediately evaluates `bin[0]` at line 105. That byte is the unwritten heap byte returned by `UA_unbase64()`, matching the saved `MemorySanitizer: use-of-uninitialized-value` at `deps/base64.c:105:21`.

allocation_context.note: The MSAN origin stack reports that the poisoned value was created by the heap allocation in `UA_unbase64` at line 140. On the witnessed path that allocation size is exactly one byte because `UA_unbase64()` computes `*flen == 1` for the 2-character body token.

cross_validation.root_cause_matches_allocation_context: Yes — the MSAN origin and the traced root cause are both inside `UA_unbase64`: the allocation context is the one-byte heap buffer at line 140, and the traced root cause is that the later decode loop and tail logic return that buffer with `cb` still 0 and `bin[0]` unwritten.
cross_validation.patch_resolves_note: The staged patch replaces the vulnerable base64 implementation, eliminating the len==2, pad==0 decode path that returned a partially initialized output buffer.

format.contract: The staged PoC is the exact 21-byte ASCII string `{"Body""  "}"Type"15 `, and no broader input class is asserted. On the witnessed path it tokenizes as `JSMN_OBJECT(size=2)`, `"Body"`, `"  "`, `"Type"`, `15`; `Variant_decodeJson()` first recovers `searchResultType = 4` from the later `"Type"` / `15` tokens and parses `Type == 15`, then recovers `searchResultBody = 2` from the first in-object string; `decodeFields()` uses the same `objectCount == 2` to decode the body through `ByteString_decodeJson()` and then consume the later `Type` field so `UA_decodeJson()` returns `GOOD`; `ByteString_decodeJson()` calls `UA_unbase64()` on the 2-character body with no trailing `=` padding; and `UA_calcSizeJson()` immediately re-encodes the resulting one-byte ByteString, causing `UA_base64()` to read the unwritten output byte.
